import html from typing import List # Example forum post format. The placeholders {title}, {body} and {points} # will be replaced by the function below. Feel free to modify this template # as needed for your forum system. FORUM_POST_FORMAT: str = """

{title}

{body}
{points}
""" def create_forum_entry(title: str, body: str, points: List[str]) -> str: """ Assemble a sanitized HTML forum post from the given title, body and discussion points. Parameters ---------- title : str The forum post title. body : str The main content of the post. May contain line breaks. points : List[str] A list of discussion points/options, each represented as a markdown string. The function will render them as an unordered list. Returns ------- str A fully formatted and HTML‑escaped forum post ready for display. Raises ------ ValueError If any of the inputs are not of the expected type. """ # Basic type checks if not isinstance(title, str): raise ValueError("title must be a string") if not isinstance(body, str): raise ValueError("body must be a string") if not isinstance(points, list) or not all(isinstance(p, str) for p in points): raise ValueError("points must be a list of strings") # Escape user input to prevent XSS escaped_title = html.escape(title, quote=True) escaped_body = html.escape(body, quote=True).replace("\n", "
") # Render discussion points as an unordered list if points: escaped_points = "\n".join( f"
  • {html.escape(point, quote=True)}
    • " for point in points ) points_html = f"\n
      \n{escaped_points}\n
    " else: points_html = "" # Substitute placeholders in the template formatted_post = FORUM_POST_FORMAT.format( title=escaped_title, body=escaped_body, points=points_html ) return formatted_post.strip()
